Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

hope verb and noun

also I hope, I hope so, hopefully

classical

Cic. Lael. 15: memoriam spērō sempiternam fore (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 154

spērō, spērāre, spērāvī, spērātum

verb, first conjugation

hope (for); hope that

What one hopes for in the accusative, or in an accusative and infinitive, usually future (spērō tē ventūrum esse). Ut spērō, “I hope”, is said in passing: sed, ut spērō, valēbis (Cic. Att. 7.2.6).

Other words

  • 1speī: short e in the genitive (Lewis & Short spēi). De Vaan 580 heads the entry spēs, speī. After a consonant the e of the fifth-declension genitive is short: Lewis & Short itself prints fidĕi, and gives rēi only for Lucretius (s.v. rēs).

    spēs1, speī f. — hope

    noun, fifth declension · classical · Cic. Att. 9.10.3: ut aegrōtō, dum anima est, spēs esse dīcitur; Traupman 154

    Spem habēre, have hope; losing it is dēspērāre (Traupman 154).

Examples

  • jam tē vidēbō et quidem, ut spērō, dē viā rēctā ad mē

    I’ll see you soon, and straight from the road to my house, I hopeCic. Att. 12.2.2

  • nātō fīliō pater spem dē illō prīmum quam optimam capiat

    when a son is born, let the father first form the highest hopes of himQuint. 1.1.1

  • dēsine fāta deum flectī spērāre precandō

    stop hoping to bend the decrees of the gods by prayingVerg. A. 6.376

See also wish, wait.
